To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated a new scatter imaging technique, coded aperture coherent scatter imaging (CACSI), which is able to reconstruct 3-D images of breast tissue and automatically identify the cancerous tissue in the tissue samples.

a scatter imaging technique has been developed for the identification of cancerous and normal breast tissue samples and that this technique has the potential to identify cancerous tissue inside a heterogeneous sample in a time on the scale of a minute per sample.

coded aperture scatter spectral imaging can reconstruct images of breast samples and identify the cancerous tissue inside them with a sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and false negative rate of 92.3%, 91.7%, 92.0% and 7.7%, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a scatter imaging technique that can differentiate cancerous and normal tissues within breast tissue samples in a single snapshot acquisition, without the need of rotation of the samples.
the development of a new scatter imaging technique for breast tumor detection that has potential for intraoperative margin assessment.
the design and implementation of coded-aperture scatter imaging for the differentiation of breast tissue samples in a heterogeneous sample.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a scatter imaging technique that can differentiate between cancerous and healthy samples and reconstruct 3-D images of the sample.
the coded aperture scatter imaging technique is able to reconstruct 3-D images of breast samples and identify the cancerous voxels in them with high accuracy.
coded aperture scatter spectral imaging is a viable method for cancerous and healthy tumor classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coded aperture coherent scatter imaging technique is a promising method for tumor classification in heterogeneous breast tissue samples.
the technique is feasible for tumor classification in breast tissue samples and has the potential to be used for intraoperative assessment during lumpectomies.

we have shown that the technique can differentiate cancerous and normal tissue in a heterogeneous breast tissue sample with a sensitivity and specificity of 92.0% and 91.9% respectively, and that the technique can provide scatter images that are highly correlated to x-ray diffraction measurements of the same tissue samples.

the technique has the potential for intraoperative margin assessment and could potentially be used to identify the presence of cancerous tissue inside a sample with a sensitivity and specificity of approximately 90%.
the technique has the potential to be developed into an intraoperative tool for breast cancer lumpectomy margin assessment.
